title: Slave Trade Act 1807 (Britain)
summary: On 25 March 1807, King George III gave royal assent to the Slave Trade Act, prohibiting British vessels and subjects from participating in the transatlantic slave trade from 1 May 1807. Passed by the British Parliament after decades of campaigning by abolitionists and continuous resistance by enslaved peoples, the statute dismantled the world's largest commercial slave trafficking fleet and initiated international naval interdiction, though legal chattel slavery in British colonies persisted until the 1833 Emancipation Act.

uncertainty.note: Royal Assent given on 25 March 1807; trading prohibited from 1 May 1807.
